title: Notice-Age Rates in Compromise Measurement — Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery
content:
The age of a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery** sets a notice rate when the lump sum of a compromise offer is measured.

**Rule.** When the notice is older than the collection-hold window but no more than 365 calendar days old and the debt carries no fraud, misrepresentation or bad faith finding, the one-year notice rate of 97 percent applies. When the notice is more than 365 calendar days old and there is no such finding, the older notice rate of 94 percent applies. Otherwise no notice rate applies.

The collection-hold window is 30 calendar days for every debt type: Education Overpayment (Chapters 30, 35 and 1606), Post-9/11 GI Bill Housing and Books Overpayment, Post-9/11 GI Bill Tuition and Fees Overpayment, Disability Compensation Overpayment, Veterans Pension Overpayment and Home Loan Guaranty Debt. The notice age is counted in calendar days from the notice date on the debt record to today; the finding is read from the debt record. The notice rate is a percentage of the recovery remaining after the cost deduction, acting on that one figure before the limit to the balance and the final rounding.

| Notice age | Finding on the debt | Notice rate |
|---|---|---|
| 30 days or less | No | None |
| 31 to 365 days | No | 97 percent |
| More than 365 days | No | 94 percent |
| Any | Yes | None |

**Boundary cases (hypothetical).** Notice 30 days old: none. 31 days: 97 percent. 365 days: 97 percent. 366 days: 94 percent.
